To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the product type is a key driver of reverse logistics arrangements and that reverse logistics arrangements are not static, rather they change from one stage to another as the product moves across its product life stages.
the reverse logistics channels are not static in nature and they change as the products move through their life stages.

the products with similar supply chain member motivations can be grouped into six types, which are: 1) product type 1: product is returned by the customer for a refund; 2) product type 2: product is returned to the retailer by the customer; 3) product type 3: product is returned due to a defect; 4) product type 4: product is returned because it is obsolete; 5) product type 5: product is returned as a result
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of reverse logistics arrangements for products that share similar supply chain members’ motivations.
the reverse logistics design implications of the various types of products sharing similar supply chain member motivations and the implications for logistics network planners.
the design and management of reverse logistics channels and provides a framework for reverse logistics network planning, based on the product characteristics and supply chain member interests.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, reverse logistics arrangements change as the product type changes and the product types can be categorised on the basis of the common motivations of supply chain members.

, the knowledge drawn from the reverse logistics arrangements within one industry or sector can be shared with another industry or sector, on the basis of the product types, which share similar supply chain members interests.
reverse logistics arrangements can vary across industries or sectors, within the same economy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this research has provided a framework to share the learning outcome of a reverse logistics arrangement, across dissimilar sectors and industries within an economy, which can be applied by logistics network planners.
the reverse logistics arrangement can be categorised on the basis of the origin of returns and reason for return and the products can be grouped on the basis of their supply chain member interests.

the knowledge drawn from reverse logistics arrangements of one sector/industry, can be applied to a similar type of reverse logistics arrangement in another sector/ industry by focusing on product types sharing identical motivations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

reverse logistics arrangements can change from one type of arrangement to another as a consumer product moves across its product life stages, and hence, the logistics planners need to design the reverse logistics channels accordingly, so that the reverse logistics objectives can be met effectively.
the reverse logistics arrangement is a dynamic process and the product characteristics play a major role in deciding the reverse logistics arrangements.

the product types can be classified based on the supply chain member interests, and the reverse logistics arrangements for a product type in one sector or industry can be applied to that of another sector or industry, provided the product types share similar supply chain interests.
